notes.7: In this exercise candidates are required to transfer information from the text provided, total accuracy is required when filling in the person’s contact details. Generally, candidates did not face any difficulty in finding the correct information for completing the form. Our repeated request has been to ensure while writing the address candidates always follow the correct order. For instance, first mention the house number then the apartment name and then the city name. This year most of the candidates correctly wrote the address. Very few candidates still made these mistakes. Exercise 3 Questions 8–11 The topic of this year’s text was about a folk theatre form called ‘Swang’ which is losing its popularity in recent times. It was pleasing to see that most of the candidates did very well in this exercise.
notes.8: The first heading under which candidates had to write required them to come up with two points about the characteristics of the folk form ‘Swang’. Most of the candidates mentioned two correct characteristics of the form.
notes.9: The next heading was about the historicity of this form. Again most of the candidates gave two correct points under this heading.
notes.10: The heading was about the significance of the form and why it is still an important form of entertainment. The candidates had no difficulty in providing the right points in this heading too.
notes.11: Few candidates did not manage to answer this question correctly: ‘Swang’ lost its popular appeal because politics has taken its role. Exercise 4
notes.12: In this summary-writing exercise up to six marks are available for Content and four marks for Language. This year most candidates appear to be well-prepared for the requirements of this exercise and generally performed well. Many candidates wrote their summaries in their own words and were therefore able to access the full range of marks available for Language. Most of the candidates had written precisely covering 5 or 6 correct points from the text. They also managed to secure 3 marks for Language and a few candidates scored full marks for Language. Majority of the candidates restricted their answer to the word limit. However, a small minority of candidates still exceeded the word limit. Section 2 Exercise 5 Questions 13–20 The text was about a woman who organised taxi drivers union in the city of New York. This year most of the candidates performed very well in this exercise. Most candidates answered correctly true/false type of questions (13–16) and were able to correct the false statements. Very few candidates gave an incorrect reply to the Question 15 as true whereas this statement was false. Most of the candidates gave correct statements for Questions 17–20 . Some candidates wrote justifications for the questions which they ticked as true. According to the rubric, if the given statement is correct there is no need to write anything or to mention the justification. Exercise 6 This year’s essay topic was on whether sport is essential for the development of a well rounded personality. Most of the candidates attempted the exercise successfully. Several candidates gave reasons in favour of playing sports and talked about its benefits, for example, improving the team’s work and spirit. More time should be devoted to teaching the basic mechanics of writing in Hindi. Sometimes frequent spelling errors hindered the meaning and made it difficult to understand what candidates were trying to say. This year, several candidates made spelling and grammatical mistakes. The spelling mistakes were threefold in nature. First, the use of the vowel sounds ‘Ee’ were used incorrectly. Secondly, the aspirated letters were written with non aspirated letters in Hindi. Thirdly, the conjunct in Hindi especially with the letter ‘Ra’ was not used correctly. Teachers should encourage their candidates to think in Hindi because some of the sentence constructions were written in Hindi however it sounded as if candidates planned what they were going to write in English and then translated their thoughts into Hindi. This caused problems with the syntax of their writing; for example, some candidates used the word in Hindi for “clever” whereas the same word has a negative connotation in Hindi and was not appropriate in the context it was used. notes.key_messages: ● In Exercises 1, 3 and 5 the emphasis is on reading skills and spelling errors are tolerated provided they do not interfere with the communication of the correct answer. Candidates are not required to write in full sentences to score the mark so long as the answer is clear. ● In Exercise 2, complete accuracy is required when filling in the person’s contact details. ● In Exercises 4 and 6 marks are awarded not only for content but also for accuracy of language and therefore it is important for candidates check their work carefully for spelling and grammatical errors.
notes.general_comments: The majority of candidates performed well in this year’s examination. The candidates followed the guide lines appropriately and most of them had written their answers within the word limit. Many candidates answered questions in Exercises 1, 2, 3 and 4 correctly.
